title: SLO exception — customer playback and action plan (Oct 2027)
summary: On 2027-10-11 at ~03:14 UTC we observed a sustained SLO exception for the hosted text-generation route in us-west-2 that affected 8% of requests for ~90 minutes. The user-visible symptom was elevated tail latency and sporadic 504s for multi-turn chat routes. This doc contains an immediately publishable status update, a customer-facing post-incident narrative, recommended actions for integrators, and the internal action plan and owners.
customer_facing_status_page_text: Status: Partial degradation affecting text generation in US-West (hosts us-west-2). Impact: increased tail latency and intermittent 504s for multi-turn chat and long-sequence generation. Mitigation: traffic rerouted to warmed fallback pool and aggressive short-term scaling applied; partial recovery underway. ETA for full recovery: under 2 hours. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and guidance for integrators.
customer_postmortem_summary: What happened: Between 03:10–04:40 UTC we experienced an SLO exception where the 99th percentile server-side latency climbed above our target for the text-generation API in us-west-2, and a subset of requests returned 504. Why it happened (short): an untested kernel selection path for long-context workloads was triggered by a coordinated traffic pattern following a large model rollout. The selection path caused suboptimal memory allocation on several GPU nodes and led to CPU-side dispatcher backlog and timeouts. What we did: rolled traffic to a verified warm fallback pool, paused the rollout, and applied a conservative kernel override to affected nodes. Impact to customers: 8% of requests in the region experienced higher latency or failed; most customers saw degraded tail latency only. What you should do: if you rely on strict P99 latency, consider enabling region fallback and pins to specific model builds; adopt client-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter for idempotent requests. Our commitments: a detailed root-cause postmortem, permanent remediation plan, and SLA review with credits where appropriate.
timeline: 2027-10-11 03:10 UTC — An alert: P99 latency breach for text-gen route in us-west-2
2027-10-11 03:14 UTC — Initial assessment: increased dispatcher queue depth and growing CPU load on several serving nodes
2027-10-11 03:25 UTC — Mitigation: shifted 40% of traffic to warm fallback pool (verified) using routing policy 'latency-protect')
2027-10-11 03:33 UTC — Mitigation: paused model rollout that correlated with traffic spike
2027-10-11 03:45 UTC — Applied temporary kernel override to affected hosts; observed P99 improvement
2027-10-11 04:10 UTC — Continued rollout hold and scaling applied; 504 rate reduced to <0.2%
2027-10-11 04:40 UTC — Region back to within SLO bounds; monitoring for recurrence
root_cause: A new model variant (v2027-10-11-c) exercised a rare kernel-selection code path for long-context decoding. That path previously had limited load coverage in our preproduction tests and led to suboptimal memory fragmentation on certain GPU models, causing increased GPU-to-CPU coordination latency and dispatcher backlog which triggered request timeouts.
immediate_mitigations: Rerouted traffic away from affected GPU pool to a verified warm fallback pool
Paused the model rollout correlated with the spike
Applied a conservative kernel override to force previously stable code path on affected hosts
Increased short-term autoscale limits for the region while monitoring
permanent_remediation: Add kernel-selection integration tests covering long-context decoding across representative GPU types
Improve pre-rollout traffic shaping to gradually exercise rarely-hit code paths under controlled load
Enhance memory-fragmentation telemetry and automated host draining when frag exceeds thresholds
Formalize rollout gating that requires baseline P99 checks across region and model variants before 50% rollouts
customer_actions_and_recommendations: Enable region fallback (recommended for latency-sensitive integrations): route to eu-west-1 or us-east-1 if us-west-2 P99 > threshold
Pin to a verified model variant for production-critical routes if deterministic latency is required
Implement client-side retry with exponential backoff + jitter for idempotent generation calls (recommended max 3 retries)
Consider shorter max-output-token limits or early-stopping heuristics for long-sequence workloads to reduce server-side execution time
If using streaming, set a conservative chunk timeout (e.g., 10s) and treat chunk failures as recoverable
compensation_and_sla_notes: We will evaluate affected customers for SLA credits per account impact. Customer-success will proactively reach out to customers with sustained usage or contracts to review credits and remediation steps. Affected customers may expect individual outreach within 72 hours.
